title: The Trapezium cluster
caption: The Orion Nebula and Trapezium cluster, imaged by the Danish 1.54-metre telescope at La Silla
credit: ESO/IDA/Danish 1.5 m/R.Gendler, J.-E. Ovaldsen, and A. Hornstrup

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Clouds of glowing gas in many colours and shapes spread across this picture of the Orion Nebula, also known as Messier 42. It is one of the great star-forming nurseries in our part of the Milky Way.

The nebula holds enough gas to make 10,000 suns. It is mostly hydrogen, with helium, carbon, nitrogen and oxygen in decreasing amounts. At its heart sits the Trapezium, four extremely hot stars whose light makes the nebula shine. They are the brightest members of a sprawling cluster of several thousand young stars, many of them hidden inside the opaque gas and dust.

The Orion Nebula is easy to find with the unaided eye, yet there is apparently no written record of it before the 17th century. The image was made with the 1.5-metre Danish telescope at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile.

understand.summary: The Danish 1.54-metre telescope took this visible-light image through B, V and R filters. The colour mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The nebula is visible to the naked eye as a faint patch, but its colours and detail only appear in telescope exposures.

explore: The picture combines three filters, with B for 60 seconds, V for 30 seconds and R for 21 seconds. East is at the upper right and north at the lower right. The nebula lies about 1,500 light-years away.
alt: Colourful clouds of glowing gas in many shapes, lit by a group of hot stars.
